notes: This inventory is based on static file and source-code patterns only.
API routes are best-effort detections and may miss dynamic routes or framework-specific routing.

findings.title: Environment file committed or deployed
findings.note: This file often contains passwords, API keys, database URLs, and production secrets. If it is exposed or committed, attackers may be able to access real services.
findings.evidence: File named .env exists. Content is not printed to avoid exposing secrets.
findings.description: An environment file can contain application secrets and credentials.
findings.remediation: Remove it from the repository/deployment and rotate any exposed secrets.

findings.title: .git directory present
findings.note: A .git folder can expose source history, old secrets, deleted files, branches, and commit metadata. It should never be web-accessible or deployed as part of a public app.
findings.evidence: Directory named .git exists in the scanned tree.
findings.description: A Git metadata directory is present under the scanned tree.
findings.remediation: Do not deploy .git directories to web-servable or production paths.

findings.title: Database dump file present
findings.note: Database dump files may contain real user data, passwords, emails, tokens, or internal records. Leaving them in a code or web folder is high risk.
findings.evidence: File extension .sql found at backend/scripts/supabase_schema.sql.
findings.description: SQL dump files often contain sensitive production or staging data.
findings.remediation: Remove database dumps from deployed/source paths and store backups securely.

findings.title: Wildcard CORS origin configured
findings.note: Wildcard CORS can allow untrusted websites to read browser-accessible API responses in some setups.
findings.evidence: Static pattern matched on line 35. Sensitive values are not printed.
findings.description: Wildcard CORS can expose browser-readable API responses to untrusted origins in some deployments.
findings.remediation: Restrict CORS origins to trusted domains and avoid credentials with wildcard origins.

findings.title: Code appears to log secret or token data.
findings.note: Secrets written to logs can leak through log files, dashboards, backups, or support bundles.
findings.evidence: print(f"GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN={creds.refresh_token}")
findings.description: Rule python-logging-secret matched this source location.
findings.remediation: Do not log passwords, tokens, authorization headers, or secret values.
